questions.text: In an undirected connected planar graph G, there are eight vertices and five faces. The number of edges in G is _________.
questions.solution:
Euler's formula for a connected planar graph: V [latex]-[/latex] E + F = 2.

8 [latex]-[/latex] E + 5 = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] E = 11

Answer: 11

questions.text:
Consider the following undirected graph with edge weights as shown:

The number of minimum-weight spanning trees of the graph is __________
questions.solution:
Take all 0.1 edges first (Kruskal). They form no cycle and split the graph into two trees: the top row (3 vertices) and the bottom 6 vertices.

To join these two parts we need one 0.9 edge; the three vertical edges from the top row down to the middle row all cost 0.9. Any one of them works.

Answer: 3

questions.text: The lifetime of a component of a certain type is a random variable whose probability density function is exponentially distributed with parameter 2. For a randomly picked component of this type, the probability that its lifetime exceeds the expected lifetime (rounded to 2 decimal places) is _________
questions.solution:
Exponential with [latex]\lambda=2[/latex]: mean = [latex]\frac1\lambda=\frac12[/latex], and [latex]P(X \gt x)=e^{-\lambda x}[/latex].

[latex]P\left(X \gt \frac12\right)=e^{-2\cdot\frac12}=e^{-1}\approx0.37[/latex]

Answer: 0.37

questions.text:
There are 6 jobs with distinct difficulty levels, and 3 computers with distinct processing speeds. Each job is assigned to a computer such that:

The fastest computer gets the toughest job and the slowest computer gets the easiest job.
Every computer gets at least one job.

The number of ways in which this can be done is ___________.
questions.solution:
The toughest job goes to the fastest and the easiest to the slowest. The other 4 jobs can go to any of the 3 computers: [latex]3^4=81[/latex] ways.

The middle computer must get at least one job; remove the cases where all 4 go to the other two: [latex]2^4=16[/latex].

81 [latex]-[/latex] 16 = 65

Answer: 65

questions.text:
Consider the following expression.
[latex]\lim_{x\rightarrow-3}\frac{\sqrt{2x+22}-4}{x+3}[/latex]
The value of the above expression (rounded to 2 decimal places) is ___________.
questions.solution:
At x = [latex]-[/latex]3 the numerator is [latex]\sqrt{16}-4=0[/latex] (form 0/0). Use L'Hospital:
[latex]\frac{d}{dx}\sqrt{2x+22}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x+22}}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] at x = [latex]-[/latex]3: [latex]\frac14=0.25[/latex]

Answer: 0.25
